title: Rajnath Singh Offers India's Battle-Tested Counter-Terror Expertise to ASEAN Partners
excerpt: At the ADMM-Plus conclave in Cebu, the defence minister cited Operation Sindoor and offered joint exercises, capacity-building and intelligence sharing to regional partners.
body:
• Defence Minister Rajnath Singh told the ADMM-Plus conclave in Cebu on October 29 that India is fully prepared to share its battle-tested counter-terrorism expertise with ASEAN and dialogue partners.
  • He cited Operation Sindoor as proof of India's proactive doctrine against state-sponsored terror, offering joint exercises, capacity-building and intelligence sharing.
  • India and Malaysia are co-chairing the ADMM-Plus Experts' Working Group on Counter-Terrorism for the 2024-27 cycle.
  • Singh also proposed a defence 'Youth Bridge' and reaffirmed India as a net security provider backing UNCLOS and freedom of navigation in the Indo-Pacific.

India is ready to share its "battle-tested" counter-terrorism expertise with ASEAN and its dialogue partners, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said on Thursday, describing Operation Sindoor as a declaration of New Delhi's clear approach against state-sponsored terrorist activities. Singh addressed the 13th ASEAN Defence Ministers' Meeting-Plus (ADMM-Plus) conclave in Cebu in the Philippines, according to The Hindu BusinessLine.

"India is fully prepared to share its practical and battle-tested counter-terrorism expertise with ADMM-Plus partners. Through joint military exercises, capacity-building programmes, and robust intelligence sharing, we can further strengthen our collective capabilities."

— Rajnath Singh, Defence Minister

Expertise earned, not theoretical

Singh said India's counter-terrorism experience is not classroom or theoretical knowledge, but experience gained over decades confronting complex, cross-border security challenges. "Every strategy of ours against terrorism has been tested and proven in actual operations," he said, pointing to last year's Operation Sindoor, when a large number of terrorist infrastructure sites were destroyed. BharatShakti reported the same formulation, quoting Singh that Operation Sindoor "decisively demonstrated India's proactive, battle-tested doctrine."

Counter-terrorism is an established workstream under ADMM-Plus. India and Malaysia are co-chairing the Experts' Working Group on Counter-Terrorism for the 2024 to 2027 cycle, IANS reported, and Singh said New Delhi wants to increase security measures in the field and eliminate the roots of terrorism.

ASEAN centrality and the Indo-Pacific

The minister reiterated that India attaches importance to ASEAN centrality and supports an Indo-Pacific that is secure, resilient and rule-based, where peace and stability are the outcome of collective efforts rather than aspirations. India's strategic engagement with ASEAN is long-term and rooted in shared interests, mutual respect and practical cooperation, he said, recalling that the second ASEAN-India Defence Ministers' Informal Meeting in Kuala Lumpur last October reaffirmed the defence components of the ASEAN-India Comprehensive Strategic Partnership and the Plan of Action for 2026 to 2030.

Maritime cooperation in 2026

Singh highlighted maritime security as a priority for 2026, which India has designated the ASEAN-India Year of Maritime Cooperation, alongside the second ASEAN-India Maritime Exercise. He said the Indian Navy has maintained an uninterrupted operational presence in volatile waters including the Gulf of Aden since 2008, escorting thousands of merchant vessels and thwarting dozens of hijackings irrespective of a vessel's flag or nationality. India will continue to act as a "trusted net security provider" in the Indian Ocean region and the wider Indo-Pacific, he said, adding that its advocacy of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) and freedom of navigation and overflight is not against any country.

A Youth Bridge and bilateral talks

Singh proposed a dedicated defence 'Youth Bridge' between India and ASEAN to promote institutional connectivity, digital innovation and capacity-building, aligning with the Youth, Peace and Security agenda. On the sidelines on October 28, he held bilateral talks with South Korean Defence Minister Kang Shin-chul and Singapore Defence Minister Chan Chun Sing, among other counterparts, covering military technology co-development, defence industry collaboration and expanded joint exercises, BharatShakti reported. He also invited Singapore's minister to Aero India 2027 in Bengaluru.
